original_question: Characterize the possible growth rates of permutation classes in the interval between κ ≈ 2.21 and λ ≈ 2.48, where κ is the least accumulation point of accumulation points of growth rates and λ is the threshold above which every real number occurs as a growth rate of some permutation class.
target_in_paper: Section 7, unnumbered open problem at the end of the growth-rates discussion: “Thus a striking problem remains: To characterise the growth rates between κ and λ.” In this survey paper, that is the nearest official formulation of your draft; it is not presented as a numbered conjecture or theorem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the paper’s actual target: the problem of determining which real numbers occur as growth rates of permutation classes in the interval from κ≈2.20557 up to λ≈2.48187. It also correctly identifies κ as the least accumulation point of accumulation points of growth rates, and λ as the value above which every real number is known to occur as a growth rate of some permutation class. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
missing_details: The paper’s notion of “growth rate” is the limsup growth rate gr(C)=limsup_{n→∞}|C_n|^{1/n}, not an a priori ordinary limit; here C_n is the set of permutations of length n in the class C.
The question should explicitly quantify over permutation classes C and define what a permutation class is: a set of permutations closed downward under pattern containment.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should define C_n as the set of members of C of length n.

The role of λ should be stated in the paper-faithful way: Vatter proved that every real number at least λ occurs as a growth rate, and conjectured that this bound is best possible; the paper does not prove that λ is the minimal such threshold.

The draft does not say explicitly that the task is to determine exactly which real numbers in that interval occur as growth rates, rather than to estimate, bound, or describe asymptotically the interval as a whole.
refined_question: Let C be a permutation class, let C_n denote the set of permutations of length n in C, and define its growth rate by gr(C)=limsup_{n→∞}|C_n|^{1/n}. Determine exactly which real numbers r with κ≤r<λ occur as gr(C) for some permutation class C, where κ≈2.20557 is the least accumulation point of accumulation points of permutation-class growth rates and λ≈2.48187 is the constant such that every real number at least λ is known to be the growth rate of a permutation class.
justification: The introduction says that Section 7 treats permutation classes and their growth rates, and Section 7 then supplies the needed local context: it defines permutation classes, defines the growth rate via limsup, recalls the significance of κ and λ, and ends by posing the open problem in essentially the same terms as your draft. Because this paper is a survey, the closest paper-faithful target is that final unnumbered Section 7 problem statement, not a broader neighboring problem about uncountability thresholds, generating functions, or finitely based classes. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
